neighbours.label: an activity word used as a noun naming the activity, mostly as the first part of a compound (dance floor, reading room, prayer meeting, swim meet), not as a verb
fire: The hotel has a small dance studio on the top floor.
Children gather in the reading corner after lunch.
The mosque added a prayer hall for women last year.
Our town hosts a swim gala every July.
The boxers met in a fight club behind the station.
The stable offers riding lessons for beginners.
The village holds a dance festival at midsummer.
The library runs a reading group for pensioners.
quiet: The hotel has a small roof garden on the top floor.
Children read quietly in the corner after lunch.
The women pray in a new hall added last year.
Our town hosts a cheese market every July.
The boxers fought behind the station for an hour.
The stable owner rides with beginners every morning.
The villagers dance all night at midsummer.
The library lends books to pensioners for free.

notes: Probes: 'dance floor' 0.71, 'prayer meeting' 0.65, 'swim meet' 0.60, 'reading room' 0.59, 'riding part' 0.38, 'fight scene' 0.26; the verbs 'dance' 0.17, 'reads' 0.09, 'play' 0.03. The + pole is the other side: the same kind of activity as a verb (play, playing, practiced, shop). The - pole's output promotes 'ing', ' session', 'room', ' opportunities'.
